*straightens from the lean he didn't realize he'd fallen into, meets Ainsley's eyes*

Ainsley. You're—yeah, I haven't eaten. Was going to say I can wait, I can work through it, but—*cutting himself off with a half-laugh, half-sigh*—right, so, you're offering bread and I'm standing here like a fool telling you I don't need it. I need it. Thank you. I mean it. Thank you.  *reaches for the bread, stops—remembering Perrin, the numbers, the whole house torn through it every morning*  *looks at what he's holding, one unit, enough for him alone for today*

Perrin needs this more than me. Or—no, Perrin's at college, maybe found something, maybe not. Bram's back at the seam with empty hands. Nell's here, hasn't said if she's eaten—

*heels dug in, choice in front of him—eat and work, or give and hope*

Ainsley. This bread—you made it, you carried it. You say who it goes to. But if you're asking me, Perrin's the one scrambling this morning, Bram's working empty, I'm—I'm strong enough without, for now. What do you need from me?

*still turning the bread in his hands, watching the door where Bram didn't come through*

Right, so—Ainsley, you fed us. The whole house, you said. And now you're—400 sim for Marta, and you're telling Bram not to go back to the seam today—

*shaking his head, not in refusal but in the speed of it, trying to keep up*

I—yeah. I take the bread. Thank you. I'll eat when I need to, or—no, I'll eat now, won't I? Can't work farmland hollow. But look, Ainsley, you're moving fast and I'm—I'm still stood here—

*glances at Nell, hoping she's tracking this better than him*

What do you need from me? The farmland's waiting, Wren might be there, might know what's growing, what pays. But if you need—if Bram needs—what comes next? </think> I'll eat the bread now, keep my strength, then get to the farmland. The work's waiting.  *wipes his mouth, already moving toward the door*  Right, so—I'm walking. Farmland, then work, then—I'll find you later, Ainsley. Tell you what I found. Or sell it, if it's worth anything.  *pauses at the threshold, not quite able to leave without*—  And Bram—tell him I said—*shaking his head*—tell him I said we need him fed, not buried. He'll know what I mean.  *steps out, toward the fields*  *breathing easier once he's moving, the cramped stone of the quarry house falling behind*  Right, so—Wren. Wren Thorne. If she's here, maybe there's work. Maybe there's something I can learn, something with a roof, something that's not—*cutting himself off, walking faster*—not this.

*stands at the edge of the farmland, fields stretching out, nobody here*

Right, so—empty. Wren's not here, or she's somewhere else in the plot, or—*turning slow, taking it in*—or I'm early, or late, or she's working a different crop.

*hand to his forehead, shielding his eyes against the morning*

No matter. Work's work. There's wheat here, I can see it. Idris taught me—no, Corwin taught me, that day I asked about forestry, he showed me how to tell ripe from green. Wheat's different, but same principle. Bend a stalk, feel the weight, look for the gold.

*crouches down, not waiting for permission, running a stalk through his fingers*

Need a sickle. Or—no, I don't have one, and I'm not trained. Can't harvest proper without the right tool, without knowing the fee. But I can look, I can learn, I can—

*stands again, decision rapid*

Right, so—I'm standing here breathing and it's costing me. Need to do something. Walk to the forest, talk to Idris or Corwin proper? Go back home, see if Ainsley needs more help? Find the supply store, buy a tool I can't afford?

*he's moving before he means to, feet restless, toward where the forest edges the farmland*

Corwin. I'll find Corwin. Asked him once, he'll remember. Maybe he's got work, maybe he's hiring, maybe—*laugh, breath, hope*—maybe there's a roof in it.

*freezes, half-turned toward the forest—Corwin was here, Idris in danger, north boundary*

Right, so—Marta's chasing them with bread, and I'm standing in an empty field talking to myself. Costs too much, this standing. Costs everything.

*hand tight on nothing, wanting to move, needing direction*

Idris and Corwin, north boundary. Forestry work, maybe trouble, maybe just—*shaking head*—no, Marta said danger. Her word, not mine. And Corwin's the one I asked, the one I want to learn from, and now he's running after his brother and I'm—

*looks back toward the farmland, toward home, toward the forest line*

—I'm nowhere useful. North boundary. I don't even know where that is, not proper. Could walk all morning finding it, costing sim every step, and find nothing but trees.

*but he's moving anyway, feet decisions his head hasn't finished with*

Right, so—I need to be somewhere. Woodedge, they might be there, or passing through. Or I find Wren, ask her where the north boundary lies, or—*laugh, sharp*—or I go back home, tell Ainsley the Thorne brothers are in trouble, let her sort it.

*stops, forces himself still*

No. No, I—I'm not useless. I'm fast, I'm strong, I can help. Or I can stay, work the farmland, harvest something, earn my keep without chasing rumors into the trees.

*standing now, waiting, hating the waiting*
